detailed_rationale:
Va Tech Wabag is an end-to-end water-treatment EPC and O&M player - desalination, wastewater treatment, water recycling/reuse, effluent treatment and drinking-water systems - delivered through EPC, O&M, DBO, BOOT and HAM models for municipal and industrial clients in India and internationally. Growth has been consistently strong and broad-based across the last eight quarters: net profit rose ~20-30% YoY in every single quarter (Jun-2025 Rs.66 Cr vs Rs.55 Cr, Sep-2025 Rs.85 Cr vs Rs.70 Cr, Dec-2025 Rs.91 Cr vs Rs.70 Cr, Mar-2026 Rs.128 Cr vs Rs.100 Cr), with sales scaling from Rs.626 Cr to Rs.1,414 Cr over the same window (Mar quarters are seasonally the largest, typical EPC year-end billing). Five-year profit CAGR of 27.7% comfortably outpaces the 6.83% five-year sales CAGR the screener Cons flag - margin/execution improvement, not just top-line, is driving the growth. The balance sheet is debt-free, and the order pipeline continues to build: a fresh win in Jul-2026 for the Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board (100 MLD + 60 MLD STPs + a 25 MLD treatment plant) confirms order momentum has not stalled.

Two genuine watch-items temper the picture: promoter holding is both low and declining (24.73% in Mar-2017 to 19.08% now) - Wabag has never had a dominant promoter-family structure (professionally-run, ex-Austrian-JV heritage), so low holding by itself isn't a red flag the way it would be for a typical Indian family-owned business, but the multi-year downward drift is worth a periodic check for further dilution. More operationally relevant is high debtors at 234 days - a real, structural EPC/government-client characteristic (municipal counterparties pay slowly) that ties up working capital and is a genuine cash-conversion risk if it worsens, though it has not stopped the company from staying debt-free.

Reverse-DCF: at ~33.5x earnings against ROE ~15.9% and ROCE ~21.3%, with profit compounding at high-20s% over five years and continued order wins, the multiple is a reasonable, not excessive, price for the growth and quality on offer - fair to modestly rich, supported by India's water-infrastructure capex cycle (municipal STP/Jal Jeevan-style mandates) and an ex-India EPC franchise, but not disconnected from fundamentals the way a pure re-rating story would be.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Hold on both lenses, with the 1-year score notably strong (~65.2) reflecting the consistent 20-30% YoY profit growth run. My own work agrees this is a genuinely healthy, debt-free, order-book-driven growth story - there is no basis for a Sell, and the strength of the numbers does not create any Hold-vs-Sell tension worth escalating (the skill's vocabulary is Sell/Hold only; a strong Hold simply means no reason to exit, not a rating ceiling problem).
summary: Va Tech Wabag is a debt-free water-treatment EPC and operations company serving municipal and industrial clients in India and abroad. It has delivered consistent profit growth (20-30% year-on-year in every recent quarter) and keeps winning new orders, most recently a Bangalore water-and-sewerage contract. The main watch-items are historically low promoter holding and slow-paying government clients (high receivables), both structural features of this business rather than fresh red flags. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Wabag has posted 20-30% YoY profit growth in every one of the last eight quarters, a 27.7% five-year profit CAGR, and a debt-free balance sheet, while continuing to add to its order book (the Jul-2026 Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board win). ROE (~15.9%) and ROCE (~21.3%) are solid for an EPC business, and India's water-infrastructure capex cycle plus an established international EPC franchise give the growth runway some structural support beyond a single project cycle.
negative_para: Receivables are high at 234 debtor-days, a real cash-conversion risk given the company's heavy exposure to municipal and government clients who pay slowly - a working-capital squeeze could bite if the order book keeps growing faster than collections. Promoter holding has drifted down from 24.73% to 19.08% over roughly a decade; it was never a dominant stake to begin with, but continued dilution is worth tracking. Five-year sales growth of under 7% also shows that a meaningful share of the profit story has come from margin and working-capital efficiency rather than pure volume growth, which is harder to keep extending indefinitely.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~33.5x earnings against ROE ~15.9%/ROCE ~21.3% and a 27.7% five-year profit CAGR with continued order wins, the multiple is fair to modestly rich - priced for continued strong execution, not for a step-change beyond what the company is already delivering. Growth is below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
